title: Silas and the Choir Revisited
premise: Isandro Nystrom, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has spent decades keeping the Ledgerhouse invisible—recording trades in impossible things while never trading in them. But when prayers to the old gods begin landing answers, the guild's clients start paying in miracles, and Isandro discovers the thirteenth moon rising over the capital is a countdown: the god Vhalor is wearing King Aldric like a crown and will consume him fully when the moon completes its turn. To save the king—and the found family of misfits who have become his true ledger—Isandro must break his own oath of silence, speak the unbinding word that cost every swordspeaker before him their voice or their life, and choose between loyalty to the guild that sheltered him and the truth that will burn it down. In the end, Isandro speaks, unbinding Aldric at the cost of his own swordspeech forever, and the Ledgerhouse reopens its doors as something new: a house that records truths instead of hiding them.
about_author: Sebastian Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who claims to have catalogued three libraries that officially do not exist. They write fantasy from a coastal town where the fog arrives on schedule and the church bells sometimes ring thirteen times.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Bell
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. On the night the city's bells ring an impossible thirteenth time, Isandro balances the Ledgerhouse books and notices entries appearing that no clerk wrote: prayers being answered. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine, the sense that invisibility is fraying at the edges.

chapters.title: A Trade in Rain
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A desperate widow trades her shadow for rain over her dying orchard—and gets it. Isandro records the transaction and realizes the old gods are taking payment directly, bypassing the guild entirely. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into personal fear.

chapters.title: The People of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter from junior clerk Wren's POV, introducing the Ledgerhouse family: one-eyed appraiser Maren, retired thief-toll collector Bramble, and mute kitchen-boy Oskar. Emotional beat: warmth and banter establishing the found family whose bonds will be tested.

chapters.title: What the King Prayed For
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Summoned secretly to the palace by Queen Sera, Isandro learns King Aldric has been praying for his dead son's return—and something answered, moving into the crown. The king's eyes are wrong. Emotional beat: horror masked by courtly composure.

chapters.title: Oath and Silence
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, with flashback. We learn what swordspeaking is: words that bind reality, and the oath that forbade Isandro ever speaking one again after a childhood catastrophe. Emotional beat: grief and guilt revealed; the reader learns why silence is both wound and armor.

chapters.title: Miracles at Market
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Answered prayers spread through the city—a blind man sees, a debtor's coins multiply—but each miracle leaves a hollowed-out worshipper behind. Wren witnesses one collapse. Emotional beat: wonder turning to revulsion; the cost becomes visible.

chapters.title: Maren's Price
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The appraiser recognizes the signature on the miracle-ledger entries: Vhalor, the god the guild was founded to imprison. She confesses the Ledgerhouse's founding sin to Isandro. Emotional beat: betrayal and reluctant solidarity between two keepers of secrets.

chapters.title: The Crown That Listens
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Infiltrating the palace chapel, Isandro speaks briefly with Aldric, who surfaces inside his own body long enough to beg: 'Don't let it finish the turn.' Guards nearly catch Isandro. Emotional beat: compassion for the trapped king; first open act of rebellion.

chapters.title: Guild of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. The guild's ruling circle votes to stay neutral and protect the ledgers above all, ordering Isandro to abandon the king. Isandro refuses quietly and begins copying forbidden pages. Emotional beat: loyalty divided; the institution reveals its cold arithmetic.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns of the Moon
chapters.summary: Oskar's POV, told through drawings and gestures. The mute boy, touched by the same magic, sees visions of the moon completing its cycle: the city kneeling, crowned and empty. He shows Wren. Emotional beat: innocence bearing terrible prophecy; urgency ignites.

chapters.title: The Widow's Shadow
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Tracking the shadowless widow, Wren finds a congregation of the hollowed gathering in the catacombs, feeding their emptied selves to something below the altar stone. Barely escapes. Emotional beat: terror, and resolve hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Unbinding Words
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Researching in the sealed archive, Isandro finds the rite of unbinding—and the record that every swordspeaker who performed it lost either voice or life. Maren offers to speak it instead; Isandro refuses. Emotional beat: sacrifice contemplated; love expressed through refusal.

chapters.title: Sera's Bargain
chapters.summary: Queen Sera's POV. The queen, half-suspecting what wears her husband, strikes a secret bargain with Isandro: the guild's cooperation in exchange for the Ledgerhouse's legal protection afterward. Emotional beat: political intimacy, mutual use, fragile trust between pragmatists.

chapters.title: Bramble's Betrayal
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. Pressured by the guild council, Bramble reports Isandro's thefts. The council seizes the copied pages and expels Isandro from the only home they've known. Emotional beat: heartbreak of found family fractured by institutional fear.

chapters.title: Hollow Congregation
chapters.summary: Wren and Oskar's alternating POV. The two go alone into the catacombs to disrupt the feeding ritual, buying time but getting Oskar marked by Vhalor's attention. Emotional beat: courage without a plan; the stakes become achingly personal.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Turn
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. With one lunar turn remaining, Isandro returns to the ruined village of their childhood to recover the original spoken oath—the counter-word hidden in their mother's grave-marker. Emotional beat: confrontation with the past; forgiveness of self begins.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Vhalor's POV (through Aldric's mouth). The god summons Isandro, offering restoration of their swordspeech and their erased name in exchange for standing aside. Emotional beat: temptation rendered intimate; the god knows exactly which wounds to press.

chapters.title: The Guild Remembers Itself
chapters.summary: Maren and Bramble's POV. Confronting the council with proof that neutrality means feeding the city to Vhalor, Maren burns the neutral ledgers; Bramble turns evidence against the council. Emotional beat: redemption; institutions broken so people can be saved.

chapters.title: Moonrise Over the Capital
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. On the final night, the found family converges on the palace through streets full of kneeling, hollowed worshippers. Sera holds the gates; Wren and Bramble hold the chapel doors. Emotional beat: unity forged in fire; every debt called in at once.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Word
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Before the crown, Isandro speaks the counter-oath. Reality tears; Vhalor is dragged out of Aldric; Isandro's swordspeech burns out of them mid-word, leaving them voice-wounded but alive. Emotional beat: climax—sacrifice fulfilled, truth finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: After the Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Aldric and Sera's POV. The king wakes diminished but himself; the queen honors the bargain, chartering the Ledgerhouse anew. The hollowed begin slowly refilling as prayers are returned. Emotional beat: exhausted tenderness; a kingdom learning to grieve and rebuild.

chapters.title: A House That Tells the Truth
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, epilogue. Voice roughened but present, Isandro reopens the Ledgerhouse with Wren, Maren, Bramble, and Oskar, writing a new founding principle on the door: nothing recorded here shall be hidden. Emotional beat: quiet hope; the found family whole, the future unwritten.
